notes: All values below are copied from the uniform n=24 aggregation recorded in EXPERIMENTS.md (2026-07-29) unless the claim states another n. Judge = Claude Opus 4.8 blind evaluation, RACE-style four-dimension rubric, median of 3 samples, 0-10; the judge model is the harness default (eval/judge.py), and per-run judge metadata (model, rubric hash, date, sample count) stays in the unpublished results/ tree. Faithfulness = fact-v2 clause-level support rate, 0-1. Every arm ran on the same base model (MiMo 2.5 Pro) and the same search backend; arms ran subsets of one shared question bank (n=24 / n=10 / n=3, shown with each claim). Judge scores drift run to run, so only same-batch deltas are comparable; absolute scores must not be compared across batches.

claims.claim: The three-stage pipeline F115 scores below the bare-agent baseline on judged quality at n=24.
claims.metric: Claude Opus 4.8 blind judge score, RACE-style four-dimension rubric, median of 3 samples, 0-10
claims.method: 24 Chinese deep-research questions run on the same weak base model (MiMo 2.5 Pro) and the same search backend for both arms; reports anonymised and shuffled before judging.
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms B,F115 --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --judge results/my_run --samples 3

claims.claim: Source-side pre-citation (F11) buys the largest faithfulness gain among the n=24 arms and pays the largest quality cost (the n=3 arms ran a different subset of questions and are not comparable across batches).
claims.metric: judge score 0-10 and fact-v2 clause-level support rate 0-1, both against the bare baseline B at n=24
claims.method: The search tool injects a stable numeric id per fetched page; the writing prompt may cite only an assigned number, never a URL, and code converts numbers into footnotes, so the model structurally cannot fabricate a URL.
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms B,F11 --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --judge results/my_run --samples 3 && python3 -m eval.run --fact results/my_run --v2 --arms B,F11

claims.claim: Independent post-hoc verification (F10.2) added to the bare baseline improves faithfulness least of the three structural arms and still costs judged quality.
claims.metric: judge score 0-10 and fact-v2 clause-level support rate 0-1, both against the bare baseline B at n=24
claims.method: A second pass audits every citation the baseline already wrote against the real fetched page content, deciding keep / weaken / replace / flag as unverified; the drafting pass is untouched.

claims.claim: F115's judged-quality advantage over the bare baseline shrank and then reversed as the question set grew, so no single figure describes it.
claims.metric: delta in blind judge score between F115 and the bare baseline B, measured within each batch
claims.method: Same arms re-run as the question set was expanded from 10 to 15 (adding e11-e15), to 20 (adding e16-e20), then to 24 after one question was removed and 5 deliberately data-rich 'hard' questions were added to rule out a soft-topic artefact. The mechanism is stable and explainable: honest disclosure of retrieval gaps is penalised by the judge more than confident glossing-over.
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms B,F115 --questions <subset> --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --judge results/my_run --samples 3

check.manual: the +0.66 / +0.12 / −0.08 progression comes from three separate batches recorded in EXPERIMENTS.md (n=10, n=15, n=24); the committed qa_data.json only carries the n=24 batch, so the earlier two cannot be recomputed here

claims.claim: Making the model maintain a key-claims registry while writing (F9.1) produced no clause-level faithfulness gain over simply prompting a citation protocol (B3).
claims.metric: fact-v2 clause-level support rate, 0-1, both arms at n=10
claims.method: F9.1 requires the model to append each claim and its verbatim source excerpt to a ledger file before using the claim. On this weak base model the ledger is not reliably maintained; judge scores were 8.13 (F9.1) against 8.04 (B3), and per-question latency ran about 3x the bare baseline's wall-clock over the same 10 questions (mean 1217 s vs 404 s; 1.3x B3's).
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms B3,F91 --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --fact results/my_run --v2 --arms B3,F91

claims.claim: Forcing one atomic factual claim per sentence on top of pre-citation reduced faithfulness rather than improving it.
claims.value: 0.55 vs F11's 0.78 on the same 3 questions (delta -0.23)
claims.metric: fact-v2 clause-level support rate, 0-1, at n=3
claims.method: F11.3 adds a structural constraint to F11 forbidding compound sentences that bundle several claims under one citation; the result is more, weaker-grounded micro-claims. Two sibling perturbations (wider retrieval budget, allowing uncited background knowledge) also failed to improve faithfulness. n=3, exploratory.
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms F11,F113 --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --fact results/my_run --v2 --arms F11,F113

claims.claim: GPT-Researcher, a mature external deep-research framework, scored well below every custom arm when pointed at the same weak base model.
claims.metric: judge score 0-10 and fact-v2 clause-level support rate 0-1, at n=3
claims.method: Arm G swaps the whole pipeline for GPT-Researcher against the same base model and, as far as practical, the same search backend. Only 3 questions were run because of search-quota and embedding-language limits, so this is labelled preliminary everywhere it appears and does not support a strong claim about external frameworks in general.
claims.repro: python3 -m eval.run --arms G --tag my_run && python3 -m eval.run --judge results/my_run --samples 3
